name: Unsolvable
description: Consider the following equation: where sign [ a ] represents the integer part of number a . Let's find all integer z ( z > 0) , for which this equation is unsolvable in positive integers. The phrase "unsolvable in positive integers" means that there are no such positive integers x and y ( x , y > 0) , for which the given above equation holds. Let's write out all such z in the increasing order: z 1 , z 2 , z 3 , and so on ( z i < z i + 1 ) . Your task is: given the number n , find the number z n .
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 40 ).
output_specification: Print a single integer — the number z n modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) . It is guaranteed that the answer exists.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.
